content.cancer_note: Cancer is a well-recognized predisposing factor for VTE. Risk varies by cancer type; pancreatic cancer, haematological malignancies, lung cancer, gastric cancer, and brain cancer carry the highest risk. Cancer is also a strong risk factor for all-cause mortality following an episode of VTE.

oral_contraceptives_and_vte.summary: Oestrogen-containing oral contraceptive agents are associated with an elevated VTE risk; contraceptive use is the most frequent VTE risk factor in women of reproductive age.
oral_contraceptives_and_vte.magnitude: Combined oral contraceptives (containing both an oestrogen and a progestogen) are associated with an approximately two- to six-fold increase in VTE risk over baseline.
oral_contraceptives_and_vte.population_impact: Absolute VTE risk remains low in the majority of the >100 million combined oral contraceptive users worldwide.
oral_contraceptives_and_vte.generation_effects: Third-generation combined oral contraceptives (containing progestogens such as desogestrel or gestodene) are associated with a higher VTE risk than second-generation combined oral contraceptives (which contain progestogens such as levonorgestrel or norgestrel).
oral_contraceptives_and_vte.other_methods: Hormone-releasing intrauterine devices and some progesterone-only pills (used at contraceptive doses) are not associated with a significant increase in VTE risk.

content.thrombophilia_note: VTE risk factors, including severe inherited thrombophilia (discussed in section 8), increase VTE risk.
